issues.subject: The freelancer year-end checklist
issues.preview: Six weeks left to make 2026 cheaper.
issues.intro: Welcome to the Sunday email. Each week: one tax or money move for people who work for themselves, one quick fact, and nothing you have to read twice. We start with the year-end checklist, because most of what lowers this year's tax has to happen before December 31.
issues.ps: Hit reply and tell me what kind of work you do. It helps me pick examples that fit.

issues.subject: Health insurance when you work for yourself
issues.preview: The Dec 15 deadline, and the deduction most people miss.
issues.intro: Open enrollment ends soon, and for freelancers health insurance is both the biggest benefit to replace and one of the better deductions. Here's how the options compare.
issues.move: Health insurance when you work for yourself
issues.fact: Freelancers: Dec 15 is your health insurance deadline

issues.subject: What a $1,000 write-off actually saves you
issues.intro: December is when people buy things 'for the write-off'. A deduction saves you your tax rate on the amount, not the amount itself. This week does the maths, so you can decide with real numbers.
issues.move: What a $1,000 write-off actually saves you
issues.fact: Don't buy a laptop just for the tax write-off

issues.subject: Your real hourly rate, worked out
issues.preview: Your $75 an hour is not $75 an hour.
issues.intro: Before you set next year's rates, work out what you actually earn per hour once taxes, unpaid admin time and expenses come out. The number is usually lower than people expect.
issues.move: Your real hourly rate, worked out

issues.subject: Freelancer emergency fund: how big?
issues.preview: Bigger than an employee's, and here's why.
issues.intro: Freelance income is lumpy, and December is often the quietest month. This week: how big a freelancer's emergency fund should be, and why it sits apart from your tax money.
issues.fact: Freelance income dries up in December. Plan for it.

issues.subject: Close out the year in 5 numbers
issues.preview: Twenty minutes, then you're ready for January.
issues.intro: The quiet week between Christmas and New Year is the best time to close the books. Five numbers, about twenty minutes, and January gets much easier.
issues.fact: Take a photo of your odometer tonight

issues.subject: Pay your Jan 15 tax in 6 steps
issues.preview: The fourth quarterly payment is due soon.
issues.intro: Happy New Year. The last estimated payment for 2026 is due January 15. Here's how to work it out and pay it in six steps, with the free calculator if you want it done for you.
issues.move: Pay your Jan 15 tax in 6 steps
issues.fact: Your 2027 safe harbor is already set

issues.subject: Safe harbor vs actual, side by side
issues.preview: Two ways to work out the Jan 15 payment.
issues.intro: There are two common ways to work out your quarterly payment: base it on last year (safe harbor) or on this year's actual profit. This week compares them with the same numbers.
issues.move: Jan 15: safe harbor vs actual, side by side
issues.fact: Don't pay your taxes with a credit card (usually)

issues.subject: Missed Jan 15? Your next 3 moves
issues.preview: Pay now, not April. Here's why.
issues.intro: If January 15 came and went without a payment, don't wait for April. The penalty is interest-like and grows with time, so paying something now still helps.
issues.fact: Skipped a quarterly payment? Pay now, not April

issues.subject: Every 1099 a freelancer might get
issues.preview: And why the totals won't match your bank.
issues.intro: 1099 forms start arriving this week. Here's what each one is, which ones you might not get at all, and why the totals rarely match what landed in your account.
issues.fact: Your 1099 total won't match your bank. That's OK.

issues.subject: 12 deductions freelancers forget
issues.preview: Including the fees you already paid.
issues.intro: Before you file, go through this list. Most of these are small on their own, but together they often add up to real money, and you already paid for all of them.
issues.fact: Your payment fees are a tax deduction

issues.subject: DIY, software or a CPA?
issues.preview: How to choose who files your taxes.
issues.intro: Filing season is open. Whether to do it yourself, use software or hire a professional depends on a few specific things, and this week lays them out so you can choose quickly.
issues.move: DIY, software or a CPA? How to choose
issues.fact: Before you file: check what you already paid the IRS
issues.ps: That's twelve issues. Reply and tell me what you want covered next and I'll plan the next run around it.
